rows.explanatory_content: Printed190.19 begins God said/they were made; commanded/created is on190.20. The words worhte and gesceapene in the candidate are plural predicate past participles with wǣron, not finite preterites. The complete base/plural display and passive auxiliary are required; the locator alone is insufficient.

The relative particle ðe does not itself change for case, number or gender. Establish its clause role from the antecedent and the subordinate verb; in ðū ðe eart, the finite verb remains second singular with the addressed ðū. A visible dictionary/citation form does not decide the relative clause’s missing object or subject.

A genitive may state the cause/ground of a reward. His weorces is for his work, dependent on the received reward; it is not a genitive object imposed by onfōn. The selected receiving object edlēane is dative.
Unrīm governs the partitive genitive goldes, a quantity of gold. The gold is not an accusative plural and the genitive does not follow merely because English uses of.

Higher numeral constructions can govern a genitive of the counted noun/measure. Teach or supply the exact higher-number phrase as a whole, including its internal case; the number’s English position is not an independent declension rule.42.2’s whole144000 phrase is coordinator-supplied.
Asking has an accusative person asked and a genitive thing requested: hine is the father/person asked, hlāfes the requested bread, and hit the child-subject. Bitt is third singular, not a command.

The people who benefit from mercy are dative plural ondrǣdendum. Hine remains the accusative object of their fearing. Cook’s omission of on those does not remove the people from the construction or turn them into a dative fear-experiencer.

The recipient of giving is dative: his bearne, to his child; reading mē, to me. In hāt mē sęllan ðā hearpan, source note164a identifies mē as giving-recipient; it does not make mē the person commanded to perform the giving.

The selected onfōn frame takes dative received thing/person: edlēane, reward; his cnihte Israel, his servant Israel. Other attested case frames remain valid Old English but must not be conflated with this selected frame.
The thing resisted is dative: ðǣm fȳre with wiðstandan. It is not an extra preposition before a normal accusative object.

Forgiveness can name the forgiven debts as accusative and the person forgiven as dative. In wē ūrum gyltendum forgiefað, debtors are dative plural; the subject is wē and the finite verb first plural. Existing u16-forgiefan-forgive supplies the lexical frame.

The marked prepositional complement is dative. Above all kings39.4 is a rank expression; upon/above his throne42.4 is positional. Case is explicitly selected here; do not infer accusative from English above or from a previously learned separate rank frame.

The marked prepositional complement is accusative. Distinguish heavens/earth above-position, temptation entered, the head on which a crown is placed, and the person spat upon. Cook expressly warns that on’s rest/motion distinction is not exceptionless, so a blanket motion diagnosis must not replace the specific selected case.

Preverbal ne and a negative indefinite such as nān reinforce one negation. Do not translate a second negative as an affirmative or replace the specified negative-concord target with an unassigned variant.

A simple present may refer to the future; a simple preterite may correspond to English simple past, perfect or pluperfect. These are contextual tense values, not a rule that every English shall/will/have must become an OE auxiliary. Every actual subject still determines person/number.

The selected reported/denied content clause has subjunctive. Wǣre in40.1 is third singular past; sīe in43.15 third singular present, but sīe in43.18 second singular present with ðū. In the reading eart is retained under Cook’s certainty exception; not every ðæt clause is mechanically subjunctive.

The not-yet-realized seeing is viewed prospectively from the former unwillingness to believe: ǣr ic self hit gesāwe. Gesāwe is first-singular past subjunctive here even though the same spelling can be indicative2sg elsewhere. Retain self and the requested final position of the verb.

Strong/weak choice follows construction independently of the stem-class table. Personal substantives and qualifying adjectives in direct address take the selected weak forms; therefore the address sequence needs wæstmbǣran/gefiðredan/Geongan/ealdan. A morphologically valid strong cell may still miss that context. Quantifier eall follows its own assigned system.
Greater is the comparative of micel, using the lexical comparative stem mār-. It is not the distinct adjective mǣre great/famous, and not a regular *micelra formation.

class_citation_boundary: Lexical class numbers identify the selected nominal/verbal system. Their appearance in a prompt does not independently teach every mood, syntax, sense or paradigm cell; use the literal declared system and the reference-position records.
